segment_findings.reason: Off-route segment 22:57–23:01 adding 0.80 km (2.19 km vs 1.38 km optimal), up to 1014 m off the optimal route. rejected_claims.reason: RD-4(b) makes a speed-band record insufficient on its own to exempt a detour; the AYE band-1 record [F10] is band data only and its 22:39–22:57 window closes at 22:57, when the off-route segment begins [F3], so it does not cover the substituted stretch as RD-4 requires.

RD-4(a) demands a traffic incident on the replaced portion of the optimal route; [F13] records no incident near the route during the trip window. The parallel-corridor band records [F11][F12] and light rain [F14] are not incidents on the replaced route and cannot substitute for RD-4(a) corroboration.

The driver statement [F9] is user-submitted content and yields to the system records: [F13] shows no incident and the [F10] congestion window ended at 22:57 as the deviation began [F3]; with no incident corroboration the RD-4 reasonable-cause defence fails.

No prior route agreement exists [F7][F8][F9], and RD-5 requires the rider's agreement to have been given before the driver left the optimal route; absent that, the segment is not exempted and RD-1/RD-2 apply.

The total +1.6 km excess [F1] is not refundable: RD-2 refunds only the unexempted segment's extra_km, and the residual difference between the billed excess [F4] and the segment sum stays with the fare.
RD-3 concerns rider-requested stops/destination changes; no such request was made [F7][F8], so RD-3 supplies no exemption route either way — the operative exemption test here is RD-4/RD-5.
Profile facts cannot alone decide the case, and RD-6's flag condition is not met: route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F16], so no account flag follows.
